In light of the FOMC’s 75 bp hike to a 3.75–4.00% target range and continued balance sheet runoff, both the FSR and the SLOOS point to tighter financial conditions that extend beyond policy rates. The October 2022 Beige Book further corroborates a softer growth backdrop: activity was flat to modest on balance, with several districts noting declines; districts such as New York, Cleveland, Chicago, and San Francisco reported weaker or slowing economic activity. Interest-sensitive sectors (notably housing) cooled markedly, while consumer spending and manufacturing were mixed. Labor markets remained tight but showed early signs of easing, and price pressures stayed elevated. Taken together, the Beige Book reinforces downside growth risks already flagged by the FSR and SLOOS, while inflation risks remain salient—tilting the overall assessment more negative than previously indicated.
